note: The library and family archive of the De Franceschi of Gologorica survive. They are in the National and University Library in Zagreb, they have been catalogued, and until September 2026 this project did not know they existed.
lead: Carlo De Franceschi told Kobler in 1876 that his great-great-grandfather built the family's house at Gologorica in 1711. What was inside that house — the books, the correspondence, the drafts of Carlo's own histories, the estate papers, the photographs — was not destroyed in 1945. It was carried to Zagreb, put in boxes, and left there for more than fifty years. It is now on a catalogue, under a shelfmark of its own, and anyone can ask for it.

rows.l: the span of the printed collection
rows.w: A Machiavelli of 1550, a Cipolla of 1555, Naldini's description of Capodistria of 1700, Tanara's household economy of 1680, Bembo's letters of 1743, an Ovid of 1753, Bonomo on the ancient counts of Gorizia of 1785

rows.l: and seven folders — the family archive
rows.w: 39 × 29 × 23.5 cm each, with a summary description of every box
«Poklon De Franceschi» — the De Franceschi Gift. Records run from PDF 0.001 to beyond PDF 0.745

archive.heading: And the archive is the part that matters
archive.text: After the books were done the family archive itself was arranged. What is in the fourteen boxes, in the paper's own words: manuscript drafts of the scholarly and specialist works of Carlo senior and of Camillo; family correspondence; personal and estate documentation; photographs and one photograph album; and pencil drawings on paper by the painter Giulio De Franceschi.
archive.why: Every one of those categories bears directly on this archive. The drafts are the working papers behind «L'Istria: note storiche». The family correspondence is the other half of the letters to Kobler. The estate documentation is the paper trail of the household that farmed the bishop of Pedena's rent. And there is a photograph album from a house this project has never seen a picture of.

steps.w: «Gologorica near Pazin, which was the centre of the political and cultural life of that district. In the house were a rich library and the family archive.»
After the capitulation of Italy the family went to Italy.

«Njihova je tiskana i rukopisna građa 1945. pronađena izbačena iz ormara i razbacana po kući» — their printed and manuscript material was found in 1945 thrown out of the cupboards and scattered about the house.
Most of it reached the National and University Library, where it stood for more than fifty years unprocessed and inaccessible, in the depots of the old building and then the new.
The first bibliographic record was entered on 15 May 2009. A second phase ran through 2014. Work on the last material to be found began on 20 January 2021.

marks.heading: They had no bookplate. They signed their names.
marks.text: Of 2,341 books, only 217 carry any mark of ownership at all — just over nine per cent. And the De Franceschi never had an ex libris of their own: they wrote their names instead, usually on the title page, often with a date and very seldom with a place.

names.w: The commonest, and ambiguous: it can be Carlo or Camillo, at least in books published before Carlo died in 1893.
Appearing as G. P. De Franceschi, G. Pietro, and G. P. de Franceschi.
One book. The only woman of the family to have signed one.
Signed with the fused spelling. The Gologorica registers carry a Maximilianus Antonius Josephus Defranceschi, born 9 January 1828, entered as mercator — a merchant.

people.heading: Four De Franceschi the collection is built on

rows.w: Politician and historian. Born in the house and died in it, eighty-four years apart.
Librarian and historian; Carlo's youngest child; author of the documented history of the County of Pazin.

Painter, and new to this archive. He illustrated Giuseppe Caprin's «Il Trecento a Trieste», and the copy in the family library carries Caprin's own hand: «A Giulio De Franceschi diligente ed amoroso illustratore di questo libro». His pencil drawings are in the archive boxes. He died at Gologorica in 1942 — the last of them in the house.
Lawyer and historian; Camillo's son. Three generations of historians from one house.

house.heading: What the house was
house.text: Seventeen of the twenty stamped bookplates in the collection belong to one man: Tomaso Luciani of Labin, 1818–1894, antiquarian, publicist and politician. And the reason his books are there is the reason the house matters — Luciani was a friend of Carlo's, and at Carlo's house in Gologorica he met the representatives of the Italian bourgeois, liberal and national opposition. The books are mostly seventeenth- and eighteenth-century; eight of them are Cicero.
house.then: The dedications point the same way. Books inscribed to Pietro Kandler, the father of Istrian historiography; to the archaeologist Alberto Puschi; to the politician Giorgio Pitacco; five of them to Andrea Amoroso of Rovinj. Among the authors doing the inscribing are the priest and polymath Petar Stanković of Barban and Attilio Hortis of Trieste. A farmhouse on a hill in the middle of Istria was on the circuit.

ask.heading: What to do about it
steps: Write to the Nacionalna i sveučilišna knjižnica u Zagrebu and ask for the box list of the De Franceschi family archive — the summary description of all fourteen boxes and seven folders already exists.
Ask specifically for the family correspondence and for the photograph album. This project has never seen a photograph of the Gologorica house.
Ask whether the estate documentation includes anything on the lease of the bishop of Pedena's «affitto fermo», which Carlo says his family held until the bishopric was suppressed.
Anita Marin of the NSK catalogued the collection and wrote the paper. She is the person who knows what is in those boxes.
And search the NSK catalogue for shelfmark PDF directly — 2,480 records are already public.
ask.drafted: The letter in the project repository at requests/nsk-de-franceschi-archive.md has been rewritten. The box list it was going to request turned out to be published already — so it now asks for the things a published inventory cannot give: images of specific items, and above all of the photograph album in box 6 and the Kandler correspondence in boxes 7 to 11.
ask.caution: One thing the letter says plainly, and this archive should too: no document yet links the Gračišće line this site follows to the Gologorica household of Carlo the historian. They are two families of one surname in two neighbouring parishes. The request is made as an interested descendant of the surname and the district, not as an heir — which is both truer and likelier to be well received.

source: Anita Marin, «Oznake vlasništva i posvete na knjigama Knjižnice obitelji De Franceschi» — Marks of ownership and dedications in the books of the De Franceschi family library — Libellarium 15 (2), 2024, pp. 25–46. Original scientific paper, open access, doi 10.15291/libellarium.4520. Published by the University of Zadar.

inventory.heading: The box list, published
inventory.lead: A second paper — Marin, Jurišić and Matijaca, «Arhiv obitelji De Franceschi u Nacionalnoj i sveučilišnoj knjižnici u Zagrebu», Arhivski vjesnik 67 (2024) — describes the archive box by box. It is open access. The shelfmark is PDF 2.337, and the arrangement is fourteen boxes and nine folders. What follows is what is in them.

boxes.w: Manuscript notes, drafts of historical research and sketches. Named manuscripts: «Memorie di Carlo De Franceschi», «Camillo De Franceschi 1887-89-92», «Versi giovanili di C. de F.». Letters, including one to the mayor of Trieste of 18 October 1901 signed «La Direzione della Biblioteca Civica — C. De Franceschi», and a folder «Corrispondenza» signed with Gian Pietro's initials. Letters came from Poreč, Pazin, Pula and Gologorica, and the family often wrote jointly — one of 27 June 1879 has Faustina on one side of the sheet and Camillo on the other. And then the domestic paper: the household accounts of Moncalvo — Gologorica — for 1925–26 and 1929–30, with bills for bricks, lime, cement, scissors, oil and alcohol; a notebook «Libro di famiglia Camillo De Franceschi» keeping accounts from 1900 to 1919; and a contract by which Giulio and Camillo let the second floor of the house to the parish priest Lodovico Zváček from 15 March to 15 May 1907.

Political and propaganda leaflets, society forms, cuttings from newspapers and books of the eighteenth to twentieth centuries, maps of Europe, Istria and «Il Veneto, le Alpi carniche e Giulie», and plans.

boxes.t: Transcripts, and a note on surnames
boxes.w: Drafts and transcripts by Carlo and Camillo — archival material on the French administration of Trieste, 1809–13; notes on the surnames of families of the Trieste district; material on the national composition of Istria; and material for the argument about the Istrian Razvod, which Carlo held to be a forgery. Also a manuscript by Friedrich von Grimschitz, the Austrian district governor who ran Istria from 1849 to 1861.

boxes.t: Camillo's working papers, and the family's verse
boxes.w: Camillo's drafts: the preface to the «Chartularium Piranese», «I primordi del movimento unitario a Trieste», «L'antico palazzo pretorio di Parenzo» — and his preface to his father's «Memorie». Beside them the family's own writing: «Poesie 1889» by Armella De Franceschi, Giulio's wife; Camillo's «Versi domestici italiani»; the student booklet of Carlo the younger from the University of Padua; a notebook of Italo's from 1921.

An album decorated with flowers and birds. Mostly postcards to Camillo, at his house in Trieste, at the Civica Biblioteca, and at the family estate at Gologorica — from Koper, Udine, Florence, Pula, Poreč, Portorož, Geneva, Venice, Paris, Rome and Bombay. Postcards to his wife Silvia. One from his son Italo in Rome. And one Camillo sent from Trieste on 20 March 1906 to his six-year-old son Carlo, who was staying with his uncle Giulio at Piran. Only eight photographs, on two pages. Separately, in a card envelope, the family photographs: several portraits of Carlo, a photograph of his bust at Pazin, signed school photographs from Trieste — and one woman, inscribed on the back «Maria De Franceschi, Parenzo, 187[?]».

boxes.t: The correspondence — five boxes of it
boxes.w: Private and business letters, kept in separate runs. Camillo's is the largest. Then Camillo's letters to his sister Faustina between 1886 and 1893; Vittorio's letters; and — the one this archive would open first — «Lettere archeologiche a Pietro Kandler», Carlo's long and rich correspondence with the Trieste historian. Among the other correspondents: Attilio Hortis, Ugo Inchiostri, Andrea Amoroso, Antonio Pogatschnig, Piero Pillepich, Francesco Salata, the philologists Matteo Bartoli of Labin and Giuseppe Vidossich of Koper, and Antonio Alisi.

Four envelopes of personalia, each titled: «Attestati e Documenti personali di Carlo De Franceschi da Moncalvo di Pisino storiografo istriano (1809-1893)»; «Documenti personali di Camillo de Franceschi»; «Attestati e documenti personale di Gian Pietro de Franceschi (1854-1884)»; and «Attestati e documenti personale di Giulio de Franceschi pittore accademico (1856-1942)». With them a rolled printed plan by the architect Giuseppe Hirsch — «Cappella della famiglia di Carlo de Franceschi nel cimitero di Moncalvo di Pisino», the family chapel in the cemetery at Gologorica — and a number of Giulio's pencil drawings.
Promotional material, blank postcards, reproductions of small pictures, cut-out illustrations and newspaper clippings.

folders.w: Thirty-six torn leaves of an older book printed in Italian and Latin side by side; a folded sheet with an embroidery pattern; two posters — the Italian Exposition of 1861 and the Trieste war exposition of 1917; five Lega Nazionale calendars for 1911, 1913, 1914, 1924 and 1925; and an older German one running from 22 September 1797 to 22 September 1799.
Thirty-four occasional pieces dedicated to Niccolò Tommaseo.

The household economy: records of income and expenditure, bills, Camillo's bank book and statements, and sale contracts — among them one of 1902 for a wood, signed by Giulio, Camillo and Faustina with Simon Rabar.

The unveiling of Carlo's bust at Pazin on 23 June 1929 — correspondence between the mayor of Pazin and Camillo, and photographs of the ceremony. With it: travel tickets, lottery slips, two postcards from Egypt to Camillo, a postcard bearing Hitler's picture (Olympia, 1936) addressed to Italo, and locks of hair in small envelopes marked 1887 and «G. O. D. F. 1884».

Death notices — Maria de Franceschi, Carlo de Franceschi, Gian Pietro de Franceschi, Elena Scampicchio, Carlo Combi — and press notices of deaths and memorials. Vittorio's letter to his cousin Camillo telling him of the death of their uncle Massimiliano. Wedding invitations. An older letter of 1789 with its seal. A list of Carlo's manuscript remains. And a kerchief with the flags of Trieste, Trento, Italy and Dalmatia.

A manuscript «Cose Istriane», dated 1850 and signed «Un Istriano»; manuscripts on parchment; poems by Silvio Benco and by Giuseppina Martinuzzi of Labin; and an occasional piece printed at Pola: «Nelle fauste occasioni delle nozze Maria De Franceschi — Luigi Salamon, Pola, 25 ottobre 1897».
Political and promotional material, incomplete parts of books, and cuttings.

inventory.span: The material runs from the eighteenth century to 1943, when the family moved to Rovinj and then settled permanently in Italy. Most of it is nineteenth- and early twentieth-century, and most of it is in Italian. The cataloguers note that nothing was thrown away — not a scrap of paper, not a note.

threads.heading: Three things in that list this archive should follow

rows.t: A De Franceschi married a Salamon
rows.w: Folder 6 holds a wedding piece printed at Pola: «Nelle fauste occasioni delle nozze Maria De Franceschi — Luigi Salamon, Pola, 25 ottobre 1897». This archive's own spine has Joannes Baptista Defranceschi of house 5, Gallignana, marrying Francisca Salomon in 1819. Salamon is a common enough Istrian name that this proves nothing — but it is the same pairing of surnames, seventy-eight years later, and nobody has looked at it.

Folder 5 has Vittorio writing to his cousin Camillo to tell him their uncle Massimiliano had died. The Gologorica parish registers give a Maximilianus Antonius Josephus Defranceschi, born 9 January 1828 and entered as mercator, a merchant; and one book in the library is signed «Massiliano Defranceschi». Three independent traces of one man.

Box 12 holds the architect's printed plan for «Cappella della famiglia di Carlo de Franceschi nel cimitero di Moncalvo di Pisino». There is a De Franceschi family chapel in the cemetery at Gologorica, and this archive has never recorded it, photographed it, or established whether it stands.

trieste.heading: And there is a second family archive, in Trieste, and it is a different one
trieste.lead: This page is about the fourteen boxes and 2,341 books at Zagreb. On the day it was written, the family sent a link that turned up another twenty-six boxes in another country. The Società Istriana di Archeologia e Storia Patria at Trieste — the society Carlo helped found in 1884 and presided over from 1886 to 1889 — holds the «Archivio Camillo De Franceschi e famiglia»: «Consistenza: bb. 26, sec. XIX–XX». Its printed guide of 2017 and its full thirty-nine-page inventory are both free to download, and this project now has both.

rows.lab: Three generations, and all three worked for the same society
rows.text: «I De Franceschi legano da subito la loro storia a quella della Società e per tre generazioni si spendono per essa.» The De Franceschi tie their history to the Society's from the first, and for three generations spend themselves on it. Carlo (1809–1893) promoter, then president 1886–1889. Camillo director from 1923 and president from 1935, editor of its «Atti e Memorie». Carlo the younger (1900–1972), a member who wrote for it. A family archive and a learned society's archive that cannot fully be separated — the inventory says so in as many words.

rows.lab: What Camillo did in 1944
rows.text: «Nel 1944 si trasferì a Venezia, salvando quanto poteva del patrimonio della Società.» In 1944 he moved to Venice, saving what he could of the Society's patrimony. He was seventy-six. That is why a substantial part of the Istrian historical record survives at all, and it is the reason the papers of this family and the papers of that society are tangled together in the same boxes.

rows.lab: A son this archive did not have
rows.text: «Documenti e fotografie strettamente personali appartenenti a diversi membri della famiglia, in particolare a Italo, figlio di Camillo, nato nel 1906 e morto, appena cinquantenne, nel 1957. Questi rievocò in alcuni saggi l'opera del padre.» Italo, son of Camillo, born 1906, dead in 1957 barely fifty, who wrote essays recalling his father's work. Note he is not the Ing. Italo de Franceschi of the Umag tablet, who died in 1944 aged sixty-eight — two men of the name in two branches, a generation apart.

rows.lab: And the Bembo marriage, dated
rows.text: «Si sono trovate anche carte relative alla famiglia Bembo, imparentata con i De Franceschi attraverso il matrimonio di Caterina con Carlo nel 1933.» Papers of the Bembo family, related to the De Franceschi through the marriage of Caterina to Carlo in 1933. This site already carries the Bembo of Gologorica; here is the join, with a year on it.

rows.lab: Camillo's own life, from the guide
rows.text: German gymnasium at Pisino, then the commercial and nautical academy at Trieste; a member of the Circolo Garibaldi and an irredentist demonstrator. Implicated in the explosion of a device at the unveiling of a monument to Trieste's 1889 dedication to Austria, he was sentenced to two years' hard imprisonment at Gradisca. Then the Biblioteca Civica at Trieste directly under Attilio Hortis, and after 1929 the provincial library and archaeological museum at Pola. «Fu un eccellente medioevalista.» The bomb and the prison are not on this site anywhere.

trieste.two: So there are two family archives, in two countries, and they are not the same papers. Zagreb has the library, the Gologorica household accounts, the photograph album, the Kandler correspondence and the architect's plan of the family chapel. Trieste has the society papers, the working manuscripts behind Camillo's publications with their drafts and proofs and the original documents he used, and the personal papers of Italo. The Rijeka and Pazin state archives hold a third and fourth body. This project had none of the finding aids in June and now has three of them.
trieste.source_trieste: «Guida al patrimonio documentario della Società Istriana di Archeologia e Storia Patria» (2017), pp. 29–30, and «Famiglia De Franceschi — Inventario», 39 pp., both at siasp-aps.org. Downloaded 7 September 2026 and held in this project's source library.

giuliodrawings.heading: Giulio's drawings are not only in the Zagreb boxes — they are catalogued in Trieste
giuliodrawings.lead: Carlo's son Giulio, «pittore accademico», the one who stayed at Gologorica and died there in 1942, worked for twenty years as Giuseppe Caprin's illustrator. That work is not lost and it is not private: it is inventoried, sheet by sheet, in the Gabinetto dei disegni e delle stampe of the Civico Museo Sartorio at Trieste, and the regional catalogue carries photographs of the drawings themselves.

rows.lab: Thirty-one initials, from a parchment of 1350
rows.text: A series of thirty-one drawings of decorated initials, made for Caprin's «Il Trecento a Trieste» (Trieste 1897). Caprin himself states in the book that they are Giulio's. The letters are copied from a medieval parchment of the Statutes of Trieste of 1350, then in the city's Archivio diplomatico. So a man from a hill village in the county of Pazin spent a season copying fourteenth-century capitals out of a Trieste statute book, letter by letter.

rows.lab: And the illustrations for «L'Istria nobilissima»
rows.text: Caprin's «L'Istria nobilissima» (1905–07) carries Giulio's drawings too, along with the landscapes, village views, peasant figures and archaeological objects he made for «Le Alpi Giulie», «Pianure friulane» and «Marine istriane». These are documentary drawings — a draughtsman sent to look at a thing and record it — which makes them a visual record of the Istria the family actually lived in, made by one of them.

rows.lab: And one sheet drawn for his own brother
rows.text: A drawing of the seal of the Triestine Arcadian academy founded in 1784, made as the headpiece for Camillo de Franceschi's essay «L'Arcadia romano-sonziaca e la Biblioteca civica di Trieste» of 1929–30. Giulio drew the ornament for Camillo's scholarship. Two of Carlo's sons, working on the same page, thirty years after their father's death.

rows.lab: Where to see them
rows.text: Civici Musei di Storia ed Arte, Trieste — Civico Museo Sartorio, Gabinetto dei disegni e delle stampe. The entries are in the Friuli Venezia Giulia regional heritage catalogue (patrimonioculturale.regione.fvg.it), several with digital images of the sheets. The portal refuses connections from this project's network, so the individual sheet records have been read only at second hand, through the catalogue's public summaries. That is a gap and it is named as one.

giuliodrawings.source_g: Regional catalogue of cultural heritage, Friuli Venezia Giulia (ERPAC), records under «De Franceschi Giulio», Civico Museo Sartorio, Trieste; consulted through public catalogue summaries, September 2026, the portal itself being unreachable from here.

trieste1869.heading: Trieste, 1869 — two men of the name, in a directory that had to be OCR'd first
trieste1869.lead: A three-hundred-and-twenty-seven-page city guide to Trieste for 1869, scanned at a hundred and twenty megabytes with no text in it whatever. Optical character recognition on this project's machine turned it into six hundred kilobytes of Italian, and then it could be searched. It is a street-and-office directory of the city, not a gazetteer of Istria — Gallignana, Pisino and Pedena appear once each — so what it can give is Trieste, and it gives two men.

rows.lab: A retired controller, living on his own means
rows.text: In the list of **possidenti e privati** — the men of property and private means, the section a nineteenth-century directory keeps for those who do not need a trade beside their name: **«Defranceschi Corrado, controllore in pens., V. Caserma 12.»** Corrado Defranceschi, a **retired controller**, of via Caserma 12. *Controllore* is a grade in the imperial financial and customs service, and a pensioned one in that list is a man who ended respectably. He is the first person of this surname this archive can put at a street number in Trieste.

rows.lab: And a merchant house, in textiles and pitch
rows.text: In the register of firms: **«Gleyre Costante (Enrico de Franceschi), in manifatture e pece, V. S. Spiridione 7.»** The house trades as Gleyre Costante; the man behind the name in brackets — which is how the directory gives the principal or the manager — is **Enrico de Franceschi**. The trade is **manifatture e pece**, textiles and pitch, and the address is via San Spiridione 7, in the commercial quarter behind the Canal Grande. Cloth and ship's pitch in one business is an Adriatic port's ordinary pairing.

rows.lab: Two more that are not ours
rows.text: **«Franceschinelli Maria, Androna Romagna 4»** and **«Defrancesco Giac., via Madon. 26»**, the latter an employee in active service in a city office. Different formations of the same root — Franceschinelli and Defrancesco — and recorded here so that the next search does not stop at them.

rows.lab: Why it was worth the trouble
rows.text: Trieste is where the Istrian and Fiume families were going in the second half of the nineteenth century, and where **Camillo De Franceschi** would live, work and keep his archive. Nothing in the book joins Corrado or Enrico to any line on this site. What the book does is establish that in 1869 there were **two households of the name living and trading in the city**, at addresses that can be walked to, twenty years before Camillo got there. The directories for other years would say whether they stayed.

trieste1869.source_alm: «Guida schematica di Trieste», 1869 — supplied as an image-only scan by the family; put through optical character recognition on this project's machine in September 2026, and the resulting text filed in the library beside the scan. Four occurrences of the root in 327 pages, all four quoted above.

acquire.heading: What to buy, what it costs, and which question each one answers
acquire.lead: The research log has carried «acquisitions» as a wish list for months. The Državni arhiv u Pazinu publishes a price list and keeps it current — the copy read here is dated 19 February 2026 — and most of what this archive has been wanting is on it, in print, for the price of a few books. This is that list, ranked not by subject but by **which open question on this site each one would close.** Prices in euro, direct from the archive that already answered this family's letters in 2021.

rows.lab: 1 · The ordination protocol of Pedena, 1632–1783
rows.text: **Jakov Jelinčić, «Knjiga ređenja u Pićnu (Prothocollum) (1632.–1783.)»**, DAPA Posebna izdanja sv. 37, 2015. **This archive has priests it cannot place.** Gian Mattia Defranceschi, whom the visitation of 1788 calls «parroco Mattia Defranceschi» of Gologorica and who signs the register «Ego Joannes Mathias Franceschi». Presbiter Philippus de Franceschi, celebrating a baptism at Gallignana on 19 March 1734. Gian Matteo, son of Gian Pietro, parish priest at Moncalvo and **canon of the cathedral of Pedena**. Petar Kruzila, archpriest of Gologorica, dead 1731. **An ordination register names a man's father when he is ordained.** A hundred and fifty years of Pedena ordinations, in one printed volume, for twenty euro.

rows.lab: 2 · The spiritual visitation of 1788
rows.text: **Elvis Orbanić (ed.), «Ignacije Kajetan Buzetski — duhovna vizitacija iz 1788. godine u Istri / Ignazio Gaetano de Buset, Visita spirituale del 1788 in Istria»**, Quaderni di «Archiva Ecclesiae» 13, Città del Vaticano 2016, 477 pp., ISBN 978-953-7640-30-9; co-published by the Hrvatski državni arhiv and DAPA. The Vatican's ecclesiastical archivists' association took a non-Italian member's book for the first time to print it. It is **de Buset's parish-by-parish visitation of the diocese of Pićan between 31 March and 31 August 1788** — the last year of the diocese — and it covers **Gologorica and Gallignana**. Translated by **Jakov Jelinčić and Elvis Orbanić**, both of whom are already on this project's list of people to write to, and both of whom work at Pazin.

rows.lab: 3 · The Umag baptisms, 1483–1643
rows.text: **Danijela Doblanović Šuran and Marija Mogorović Crljenko, «Matična knjiga krštenih župe Umag (1483.–1643.)»**, sv. 46, 2019. **This is the direct test of a problem published on this site today.** The parish church of Umag holds a canvas of **1650** carrying the arms of the De Franceschi of Umag — nineteen years before the family is supposed to have reached Istria from Crete. Either the arms were added later by a donor, or the name was already at Umag. **A hundred and sixty years of Umag baptisms, edited and printed, ending seven years before that painting, will say which.**

rows.lab: 4 · Valier's apostolic visitation of the diocese of Pula, 1580
rows.text: **Milena Joksimović (ed.), «Apostolska vizitacija Pulske biskupije biskupa Augustina Valiera 1580. godine»**, 2023. The most expensive on the list and the one aimed at the biggest hole. This archive has just opened a **southern-Istrian cluster** — thirty-one people at Pula, Fažana, Premantura, Medulin, Ližnjan and Barban, in the registers from 1667 — **and cannot say where it came from.** Valier's visitation is eighty-seven years earlier and goes parish by parish through exactly that country.

rows.lab: 5 · The urbarium of the County of Pazin, 1571
rows.text: **«Urbar Pazinske knežije 1571.–2021.»**, zbornik radova, sv. 56, 2023. This site argues at length about Gologorica's absence from the roll of 1498 and Carlo's explanation of it — «perchè ne era Dominus il vescovo di Pedena». **The next roll is the one to read**, and this is the volume of studies published for its 450th anniversary.

rows.lab: 6 · Two more, cheap
rows.text: **Mirela Slukan Altić, «Katastar Istre»** (2001) — the cadastral history of the peninsula, which is what stands behind every property this archive tries to locate. And **Biserka Budicin and Maja Milovan, «Genealoška istraživanja za početnike (primjer prakse Državnog arhiva u Pazinu)»** (sv. 59, 2024) — the archive's own handbook to doing genealogy in its own holdings, which is the cheapest way to find out what else it has.

rows.lab: And one that cannot be had
rows.text: **Sv. 23, «Pićanska biskupija i pićanština»** (2012) is marked *rasprodano* — sold out. So is Škunca's «Prošlost Crkve u Istri». Those are library requests rather than purchases.

acquire.total: **The first three come to €59.72 and would answer three separate questions this site currently prints as open.** All seven come to about a hundred and fifty-four euro. The order goes to the Državni arhiv u Pazinu, Vladimira Nazora 3, 52000 Pazin — the same address that sent this family the certified copy of Josip Defranceschi's 1863 baptism in 2021.
acquire.source_acq: «Cjenik Vjesnika istarskog arhiva, posebnih izdanja i suizdanja Državnog arhiva u Pazinu», the archive's own price list as published at dapa.hr, read at its stated currency of 19 February 2026. Imprint details for the 1788 visitation from the publisher's own impresum and presentazione, also at dapa.hr.

camillobib.heading: Camillo's bibliography, entire — and three items that answer questions open on this site today
camillobib.lead: This archive has been picking Camillo De Franceschi's titles up one at a time out of other people's footnotes. IstriaNet publishes the whole list — **forty-five entries between 1898 and 1964**, with volume and page references, assembled from the Italian librarians' biographical database and the Trieste civic library catalogue. Most of it is medieval Istria and is nothing to do with this family. Three items are not.

rows.lab: The Pula wills — with a proper citation at last
rows.text: **«Testamenti polesani del secolo XV, con alcuni cenni sulle antiche casate patrizie di Pola», *Atti e memorie della Società istriana di archeologia e storia patria*, vol. 42 (1930), pp. 167–219.** Volume 39 of the Rovinj *Atti* pointed at this without a date; here it is dated and paginated. Fifteenth-century Pula wills transcribed, with an account of the old patrician houses of the city — and this archive has just opened a southern-Istrian cluster centred on Pula that it cannot place. **Fifty-two pages, in a journal that is largely digitised.**

rows.lab: And the population of Pula, which is the same question from the other side
rows.text: **«La popolazione di Pola nel secolo XV e nei seguenti», *Archeografo Triestino* ser. 3, vol. 3 (1906), pp. 221–315.** Ninety-four pages on who actually lived in Pula from the fifteenth century onward. Camillo wrote the two standard studies of the population and the patriciate of the city where this archive's unplaced cluster lives, and wrote them a century before the question came up here.

rows.lab: And then he called the Istrian Boundary Settlement a forgery
rows.text: **«Quando e da chi sia stato ideato l'apocrifo istrumento di confinazione della Contea di Pisino con la data del 1325», *Archivio Veneto* ser. 5, vols. 30/31 (1942), pp. 104–111.** This site published, an hour ago, that **Mikula Gologorički, parish priest of Gologorica, wrote the Croatian Glagolitic version of the Istrian Boundary Settlement of 1325** — one of the founding documents of Croatian literacy, from this family's own village. **Camillo De Franceschi, of that village and that family, wrote a paper arguing that the instrument is apocryphal — asking when it was invented, and by whom.** Both things are on this site now, and they should be read together.

rows.lab: Two more worth having
rows.text: **«I Castelli della Val d'Arsa. Ricerche storiche. Con documenti inediti e alberi genealogici»** (Parenzo 1900, 246 pp., offprinted from AMSI XIV–XV) — the castles of the Val d'Arsa, the country immediately south-east of Gologorica, **with unpublished documents and genealogical trees**; it was his first book, written at thirty. And **«Ricordi di biblioteca», *Archeografo triestino* ser. 4, XXII (1959), pp. 3–76** — seventy-four pages of library recollections, which is where the man who bought the Nobile drawings at Koper in 1934 and 1941, and who shelved books carrying the ex libris «De Franceschi – Seghetto», would have written about doing it.

rows.lab: The shape of a life
rows.text: Five parts on the Castropola and the commune of Pula, 1902–04. Seven parts of the *Chartularium piranense*, the medieval charters of Piran, 1924–38. Dante at Pola twice, in 1906 and 1932. The Florentine exiles of Dante's company lending money in Trieste and Istria, 1938. *Le nazionalità in Istria*, Trieste 1938 — the year that title meant what it meant. Then, after the war and the loss of the province, Capodistria's origins, a memoir of Giovanni Timeus and Pola's journalism, the statutes of Piran, and at the last **the «Storia documentata della contea di Pisino», published at Venice in 1964, edited by his son Carlo** — the county his own family came out of, finished by the next generation.

camillobib.source_cam: «Istria on the Internet» (istrianet.org), Prominent Istrians, Camillo de Franceschi, selected works — compiled from aib.it's dbbi20 biographical database of Italian librarians and the catalogue of the Biblioteche del Comune di Trieste. Page read 8 September 2026. Forty-five entries, 1898–1964.
